author: Antonialock
body:
Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):
E1JH26 (Dmel Ccs)

Description of issue
E1JH26 (Dmel) and its ortholog O14618 (human) represent the CCS protein, which is characterized as a 'Copper chaperone for superoxide dismutase' - ie. it doesn't itself have catalytic activity.

However, E1JH26 (Dmel) gets the following catalytic annotations:

    Rhea 20696/EC:1.15.1.1 via ARBA: ARBA00049204 / UniRule RuleBase: RU000393
    Keyword 'oxidoreductase' via ARBA: ARBA00023002 / UniRule RuleBase: RU000393

Can those ARBA/UniRules be reviewed so that the catalytic terms are not applied to this chaperone protein?

I made a new ticket from #5883 for the ARBA issue
title: ARBA2GO issue: E1JH26 (Dmel Ccs)

author: Antonialock
body: @sjm41 I have annotated E1JH26 in swiss-prot so these erroneous annotations will disappear and the rule should be revised.

author: sjm41
body:
@Antonialock I just noticed that another KW2GO issue I had is actually also caused by ARBA00023002:

Q9Y153 has 'oxidoreductase activity' annotation based on UniProtKB-KW:KW-0560.
But if you look at the UP page, it says the keyword was applied based on ARBA00023002.

So, this is another example of a confusing case where the real source is 2 hops away...(FYI @hattrill)

Anyway, I just wanted to check that the edits you mentioned above will also remove the keyword 'oxidoreductase' (and thus the GO annotation) from Q9Y153?
